puzzles.success: The flood was used to remove an obstacle to a transaction already planned. The transaction did not arise only as a response to disaster.
puzzles.rationale: The distance constraint plus clearance adjacency forces Assignment–Clearance–Extinguishment. Lodging precedes Purchase precedes Assignment, and Transfer follows Extinguishment. The six-event total order is unique.

puzzles.title: A seal and its limits
puzzles.prompt: Authenticate the office seal on the original counterfoil.
puzzles.details: Combine the wax impression and seal-register rubbing. This proves the office seal; retain the separate signature evidence for personal attribution.
hints: A distinctive defect can authenticate an impression.
Align the crescent chip in the two records.
Combine Wax seal impression and Seal register rubbing.
puzzles.success: The impression is genuine. You explicitly avoid claiming that a seal alone proves who held it.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: assembled.

puzzles.title: A case a reader can follow
puzzles.prompt: Arrange Sera’s five account blocks.
puzzles.details: Use the public sitting’s causal order: event, time, authority, purpose, consequence. Every block is used once.
hints: Begin with the event before explaining who ordered it.
Time follows act; consequence follows purpose.
ACT → TIME → AUTHORITY → PURPOSE → CONSEQUENCE.
puzzles.success: The accusation becomes a sequence of claims with sources, rather than an atmosphere of suspicion.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: ['ACT', 'TIME', 'AUTHORITY', 'PURPOSE', 'CONSEQUENCE'].

puzzles.title: Print only what you can prove
puzzles.prompt: Prepare the publication proof with its citations.
puzzles.details: Combine the corrected type forme and proofing sheet. The original records remain separate from this distributable copy.
hints: Sera has set the text; the sheet holds its citations.
Take the forme and the ruled sheet from the print shop.
Combine Corrected type forme and Proofing sheet.
puzzles.success: Sera approves the proof. It says Elian operated the bypass, Rusk authorised it, and twenty-three people died; each statement has its own source.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: assembled.

puzzles.title: The clear-title premium
puzzles.prompt: Calculate the private gain shown by the acquisition account.
puzzles.details: Subtract the option cost and legitimate survey fee from the transfer payout. Enter the remaining number of crowns.
hints: Start from the 310-crown payout.
Subtract 120 and then 40.
puzzles.success: The unexplained premium is 150 crowns, paid to Rusk’s trust. The ledger ties his benefit to the cleared title.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: 150.

puzzles.title: Relief for whom?
puzzles.prompt: What does the premium establish?
puzzles.details: Use the trust ledger and accountant’s note. Do not confuse financial benefit with independent proof of the signed order.
puzzles.solution: Rusk personally benefited from the land transfer
options: The payment was distributed to displaced households
Rusk personally benefited from the land transfer
The payment alone proves every detail of the flood
hints: The beneficiary is named and the relief classification was rejected.
The ledger establishes benefit, while other documents establish the act.
Choose Rusk’s personal benefit from the land transfer.
puzzles.success: You record motive precisely. The money supports the case without being asked to prove what only the order can prove.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: Rusk personally benefited from the land transfer.

puzzles.title: The unbroken dispatch
puzzles.prompt: Reconstruct the original instruction’s chain of custody.
puzzles.details: Order receipt cards A–F by matching each recipient to the next sender. Start with the unsigned draft from the Works drafting room; end at the Public vault. Each card appears once. This tracks one document, not the later evacuation return.
hints: Find the only card whose sender is the Works drafting room. Its recipient tells you the next sender to seek.
E reaches Rusk, so C follows; C reaches Olan, so A follows. Continue matching endpoints.
E → C → A → B → D → F.
puzzles.success: The originals and linked receipts connect the instruction to Rusk’s hand and Elian’s receipt. Mara’s tracing is corroborated, not left to stand alone.
puzzles.rationale: The unique document chain is Works drafting room→Rusk→Olan→Vey→Elian→Records office→Public vault. Receipt labels along it are E,C,A,B,D,F.

puzzles.title: The price of silence
puzzles.prompt: Which account of intent survives all the evidence?
puzzles.details: Join Rusk’s occupancy acknowledgement, the signed destructive instruction, the false-return direction and his private gain.
puzzles.solution: Rusk knowingly ordered diversion to destroy claims and secure the transfer
options: Rusk believed an independently completed evacuation had been verified
Elian forged every record without Rusk’s knowledge
Rusk knowingly ordered diversion to destroy claims and secure the transfer
The flood was an unrelated accident followed by an ordinary sale
hints: Rusk acknowledged occupied houses and then forbade household checks.
His instruction names the records store and acquisition; the trust records his benefit.
Choose the knowing diversion to destroy claims and secure the transfer.
puzzles.success: The case now identifies action, authority and purpose without relying on a single confession. The originals must enter the public record, and copies must survive beyond one office’s reach.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: Rusk knowingly ordered diversion to destroy claims and secure the transfer.

puzzles.title: More than one copy
puzzles.prompt: Prepare the independent public copies for distribution.
puzzles.details: Combine the verified copy bundle and waterproof dispatch wrap. Keep the originals separate for deposition.
hints: Copies preserve access; the original preserves physical evidence.
Nadi’s wraps protect Sera’s bundles.
Combine Verified copy bundle and Waterproof dispatch wrap.
puzzles.success: The island, library and print shop each receive a complete checked set. One closed office can no longer erase the case.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: assembled.

puzzles.title: What each witness knows
puzzles.prompt: Arrange the witness accounts in the planned causal order.
puzzles.details: Arrange six witnesses under all scheduling conditions from the scope cards and corrected draft. “Immediately” means adjacent positions. Every witness appears once.
hints: Form the two adjacent pairs Rowan→Mara and Ada→Elian.
Olan goes between Mara and Ada; Sera closes. This fixes the two pairs’ order.
Rowan → Mara → Olan → Ada → Elian → Sera.
puzzles.success: The witnesses agree on their limits as well as their observations. Their differences no longer provide a convenient place to hide the whole event.
puzzles.rationale: Rowan–Mara is adjacent; Olan lies after Mara and before Ada; Ada–Elian is adjacent; Sera is last. These constraints fill all six slots uniquely.

puzzles.title: The relay’s safe path
puzzles.prompt: Find the shortest pulse sequence from COLD to READY.
puzzles.details: Use both halves of the relay transition table. Begin at COLD; each selected pulse changes the current state. Submit the FEWEST pulses that reach READY. Wrong attempts are safe simulations and consume no actual resources.
hints: Work backward from READY: it can only be reached by LONG from CHECK. CHECK is reached by SHORT from BRIDGED.
The shortest path to BRIDGED is COLD→PRIMED→CHARGED→BRIDGED. Avoid VENTED and OVERLOAD loops.
SHORT → SHORT → LONG → SHORT → LONG. States: PRIMED, CHARGED, BRIDGED, CHECK, READY.
puzzles.success: Both contacts answer. The outer wards receive the same public notice as the city centre.
puzzles.rationale: READY has one incoming edge from CHECK via LONG, CHECK one from BRIDGED via SHORT, BRIDGED one from CHARGED via LONG. The shortest COLD-to-CHARGED path is SHORT,SHORT. Thus the unique shortest complete sequence is SHORT,SHORT,LONG,SHORT,LONG.

puzzles.title: Count the sources
puzzles.prompt: Calculate the notice’s packet check digit.
puzzles.details: Use the five source packet numbers in their recorded causal order. Multiply each by position 1–5, sum, then enter the single digit 0–9 that makes the total divisible by ten. Do not simply enter the sum’s last digit.
hints: The ordered weighted products are 3×1, 7×2, 2×3, 4×4 and 6×5.
Their sum is 69. You need a digit that takes it to the next multiple of ten.
puzzles.success: The transmitted source list is complete. Recipients can ask for the same five evidence packets instead of trusting an unsupported summary.
puzzles.rationale: Weighted sum =3+14+6+16+30=69; unique digit d in [0,9] with (69+d)%10=0 is 1.

puzzles.title: A witnessed safe state
puzzles.prompt: Pair the bypass isolation hardware with its signed record.
puzzles.details: Combine the gate isolation pin and witnessed isolation tag. This records the already-secured real gate and supports the procedural reconstruction.
hints: Physical restraint and an accountable record serve different purposes.
The pin and tag belong together.
Combine Gate isolation pin and Witnessed isolation tag.
puzzles.success: The secured bypass has both a physical interlock and a witnessed record. Future operators can see who checked it and what was checked.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: assembled.

puzzles.title: The limit of this hearing
puzzles.prompt: What action can the council properly take under the emergency charter?
puzzles.details: Choose the response within the charter’s authority. A referral preserves the distinction between administrative removal and a criminal trial.
puzzles.solution: Withdraw emergency authority, preserve evidence and refer the case
options: Erase all records mentioning the flood
Pronounce a criminal sentence without an outside trial
Withdraw emergency authority, preserve evidence and refer the case
Keep Rusk’s authority until every original has been destroyed
hints: The charter allows withdrawal of delegated powers.
Criminal responsibility is reserved for the outside court.
Choose withdrawal, preservation and referral.
puzzles.success: The proposed decision has a defined legal purpose inside the fiction: protect the city and the evidence while an outside court hears the case.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: Withdraw emergency authority, preserve evidence and refer the case.

puzzles.title: The five parts of the case
puzzles.prompt: Present the evidence board as a causal argument.
puzzles.details: Arrange all five claims. Use the public sitting’s established order, with consequences following the act, timing, authority and purpose.
hints: Use ACT, TIME, AUTHORITY, PURPOSE, CONSEQUENCE.
The time comes immediately after the physical act.
Bypass diversion → 00:14 meridian → Rusk’s signed authority → Destruction for acquisition → Twenty-three named deaths.
puzzles.success: Each claim is supported by a different part of the record. The whole case does not collapse if one witness is frightened or one copy is lost.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: ['Bypass diversion', '00:14 meridian', 'Rusk’s signed authority', 'Destruction for acquisition', 'Twenty-three named deaths'].

puzzles.title: The tide defence
puzzles.prompt: Why does Rusk’s exceptional-tide explanation fail?
puzzles.details: Choose the rebuttal supported by the physical route, independent time and original instruction.
puzzles.solution: Upstream diversion preceded the tide and followed a signed destructive order
options: Rusk’s manner proves he is lying
Upstream diversion preceded the tide and followed a signed destructive order
The victims’ number alone identifies the operator
hints: A natural tide cannot explain an upstream pressure rise before its own turn.
The machine evidence agrees with a signed order, not merely a suspicion.
Choose upstream diversion preceding the tide under a signed destructive order.
puzzles.success: Rusk asks for the originals. The chair answers that they have already been deposited, and that copies are being read on both shores.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: Upstream diversion preceded the tide and followed a signed destructive order.

puzzles.title: A correction that can be read
puzzles.prompt: Correct Tomas’s entry without hiding the original institutional failure.
puzzles.details: Follow the archive correction rule, using every step once. Preserve the old writing beneath a single readable cancellation.
hints: Do not begin by erasing the entry.
The sourced replacement comes after the readable cancellation.
Retain original → Rule through false claim → Add sourced correction → Date and sign.
puzzles.success: Your father’s name is corrected in public. The old accusation remains legible as evidence of what the city once chose to believe.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: ['Retain original', 'Rule through false claim', 'Add sourced correction', 'Date and sign'].

puzzles.title: The public record
puzzles.prompt: What does the finished record owe the city?
puzzles.details: Choose the conclusion that preserves the evidence, names the people harmed and leaves responsibility open to a proper hearing.
puzzles.solution: Keep the originals, publish the sources and name every person lost
options: Replace the old story with an unsupported heroic legend
Destroy the false entry so nobody remembers the failure
Keep the originals, publish the sources and name every person lost
Preserve only the evidence that clears Iona’s father
hints: The investigation began with one name and uncovered twenty-three.
A durable correction needs sources as well as a conclusion.
Choose keeping originals, publishing sources and naming every person lost.
puzzles.success: Mara closes the register only after the last name has been read. Outside, the midnight bell’s repaired mechanism waits for its next honest hour.
puzzles.rationale: Compare the cited evidence using the explicit rule. Intended answer: Keep the originals, publish the sources and name every person lost.

characters.name: Iona Vale
characters.description: You learned to mend records after a false one drove you from home. Precise hands; less patient questions.

characters.name: Mara Venn
characters.description: A friend who preserves inconvenient records. Her disappearance began with a removed page, but the investigation must establish why.

characters.name: Rowan Pike
characters.description: A practical man who remembers every gate and avoids one particular night.

characters.name: Nadi Bell
characters.description: She remembers who travelled together, which channel was open, and who never came back.

characters.name: Sera Quill
characters.description: Her mother organised the East Reach tenants. Sera insists that every strong claim needs a source.

characters.name: Elian Ash
characters.description: Designer of a bypass whose signature appears too often in records he would rather forget.

characters.name: Ada Flint
characters.description: Keeps the old observatory open because an instrument may still have something to say.

characters.name: Dorian Rusk
characters.description: His emergency powers survived the emergency. Courteous, orderly, and very interested in which documents remain legible.

characters.name: Tomas Vale
characters.description: Your father. The official flood account blames his operation of the East Reach sluice. You have come to test that account, not merely replace it with a comforting one.

recipes.text: You tear the tissue along its fibres and brush the edge with paste. A repair should support the page, not overwrite it.
You reeve the cord through the hook and secure it with two half-hitches. The load now bears on sound fibres.
The crank screws securely into the coupling. The training mechanism can now be turned without touching a live gate.
You align the shoulders of both profiles. Their working edges differ in length and notch count; the mismatch is structural.
The lens clips into the frame. You keep the metal clear of the emulsion and let the light do the work.
The spring seats on the spindle’s flat. The model can explain the fault without altering the preserved original clock.
The page number, thread holes and torn fibres align. You support the join so that anyone can inspect why these two pieces belong together.
The tracing rests against its backing. You secure the margin, never the writing, and preserve the registration marks.
The broken crescent aligns in all three impressions. The office seal is authenticated; the signature and custody record must still identify responsibility.
You pull a proof and check each factual line against its source. The sheet distinguishes direct observation, documentary evidence and admission.
The checked copies go into separate oilcloth packets. Each recipient gets the source list and the means to request the originals.
The signed tag is secured to the isolation pin. A mechanism and a witnessed record now describe the same safe state.
